examples.en: The old clothesline wore out from the rain.
Salted seafood has to ferment well to get a deep flavor.

examples.ko: 화가 났지만 시간이 지나니까 마음이 삭았어요.
examples.en: I was angry, but as time passed my anger subsided.

examples.ko: 창고에 둔 가죽 끈이 삭아서 끊어졌어요.
examples.en: The leather strap I kept in the storage room rotted and snapped.

examples.ko: 땅속에 묻은 낙엽이 천천히 삭고 있어요.
examples.en: The fallen leaves buried in the ground are slowly decomposing.

examples.ko: 속이 아직 안 삭았는지 배가 불러요.
examples.en: My stomach still feels full, as if the food hasn't digested yet.

explain: '화가 삭다'처럼 마음이 가라앉는 뜻과 '젓갈이 삭다', '옷감이 삭다'처럼 서서히 변하는 뜻이 있어요. '썩다'는 아주 상해 버린 느낌이고, '삭다'는 시간이 지나 천천히 변하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It covers both feelings that settle down (화가 삭다) and things that slowly break down, like fermenting seafood or worn fabric. 썩다 sounds fully spoiled, while 삭다 describes a gradual change over time.

examples.en: How was this amount calculated?
The average is calculated by adding up all the scores.

examples.ko: 올해 매출은 작년보다 높게 산출될 거예요.
examples.en: This year's sales will come out higher than last year's.
I'll let you know as soon as the cost is worked out.
I organized the calculated results into a table.
I'm curious by what standard the tax is calculated.

explain: 계산이나 계획에서 값이 나올 때 써요. 주로 금액, 비용, 평균, 통계처럼 숫자와 함께 쓰고, 일상 대화보다 보고서나 뉴스에 더 자주 나와요. 직접 계산하는 사람이 있으면 '산출하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when a figure comes out of a calculation, mostly with amounts, costs, averages, or statistics. It shows up more in reports and news than in everyday talk. When someone does the calculating, use 산출하다 instead.

examples.ko: 그분은 가난한 사람들을 도운 성자로 기억돼요.
examples.en: He is remembered as a saint who helped poor people.
I met a famous holy man in India.
They say the saint lived without greed.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한 성자의 삶을 다뤄요.
examples.en: This book deals with the life of a saint.

examples.ko: 사람들은 그를 살아 있는 성자라고 불러요.
examples.en: People call him a living saint.

examples.ko: 성자 같은 사람이라서 누구도 그를 미워하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is such a saintly person that nobody hates him.

explain: 주로 종교에서 아주 깊은 덕을 갖춘 사람을 가리켜요. 가톨릭에서는 '성인'이라고 더 자주 부르고, '성자'는 불교·힌두교 등 다른 종교의 인물에도 넓게 써요. 사람을 칭찬할 때 '성자 같다'라고 하면 대단히 착하다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a person of great virtue, mostly in a religious setting. Catholics usually say 성인 for a saint, while 성자 is used more widely, including for figures in Buddhism and Hinduism. Saying someone is '성자 같다' praises them as extremely kind.

en: doing; handiwork (usually of a bad deed)

examples.ko: 창문을 깬 건 옆집 아이들의 소행이에요.
examples.en: The kids next door are the ones who broke the window.
It hasn't been found out yet who did it.

examples.ko: 경찰은 이번 사건이 같은 사람의 소행이라고 봐요.
examples.en: The police think this incident is the work of the same person.

examples.ko: 이런 장난은 분명히 동생의 소행일 거예요.
examples.en: A prank like this must be my younger brother's doing.

examples.ko: 그의 소행을 알고 나서 모두 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Everyone got angry after learning what he had done.
The fire turned out to be the work of an arsonist.

explain: '누구의 소행'처럼 잘못되거나 나쁜 일을 한 사람을 말할 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고, 그럴 때는 '행동'이나 '덕분'을 써요. 보통 '~의 소행이다' 꼴로 나와요.
explain_en: It is used to name who did something bad or wrong, almost always in the pattern '~의 소행이다'. For good deeds people say 행동 or 덕분 instead.

en: be proved by evidence; be demonstrated

examples.en: That theory was proven by experiment.

examples.ko: 효과가 실증되기 전에는 판매할 수 없어요.
examples.en: It can't be sold until its effect is proven.

examples.ko: 이 방법의 안전성이 여러 번 실증됐어요.
examples.en: The safety of this method has been demonstrated many times.

examples.ko: 가설이 실증되면 논문을 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the hypothesis is proven, I can write a paper.
I included only proven facts in the report.
The medicine's effect hasn't been proven yet.

explain: 추측이 아니라 실험이나 자료 같은 실제 증거로 확인된다는 느낌이에요. 논문, 뉴스, 연구 이야기에 주로 나오고 일상 대화에서는 '증명되다'나 '확인되다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It stresses being confirmed by real evidence such as experiments or data, not by guesswork. It appears mostly in papers, news, and research talk; in daily speech people prefer 증명되다 or 확인되다.

examples.en: The research team proved the effect through an experiment.

examples.ko: 이 주장을 실증하려면 자료가 더 필요해요.
examples.en: To prove this claim, we need more data.

examples.ko: 그는 직접 현장에 가서 문제를 실증했어요.
examples.en: He went to the site himself and demonstrated the problem.

examples.ko: 결과를 실증하는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to verify the results with evidence.

examples.ko: 실증할 수 없는 이야기는 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to believe a story that can't be proven.

examples.ko: 선생님은 사례로 이 규칙을 실증해 보였어요.
examples.en: The teacher demonstrated this rule with examples.

explain: '실증하다'는 말로 주장하는 데서 끝나지 않고 실험, 조사, 사례로 보여 준다는 뜻이 강해요. '증명하다'보다 딱딱하고 학술적이라서 논문이나 보고서에 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It carries the sense of going beyond claiming and showing something through experiments, surveys, or cases. It is stiffer and more academic than 증명하다, so it fits papers and reports.

en: leave a will; say one's dying wishes

examples.en: Before passing away, my grandfather left his last words to the family.
He stated in his will that his property should be shared among his children.
The king left his last words, entrusting the country to his son.
Do you have any last words to leave?

examples.ko: 그분이 어떤 내용을 유언했는지 아무도 몰라요.
examples.en: Nobody knows what he said as his last wishes.

examples.ko: 할머니는 병원에서 조용히 유언하고 눈을 감으셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother quietly left her last words in the hospital and passed away.

explain: 죽기 전에 남기는 말이나 뜻을 남길 때 써요. 일상에서는 '유언을 남기다'나 '유언을 하다'가 훨씬 자연스럽고, '유언하다'는 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. 높일 때는 '유언하시다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for leaving words or wishes before death. In everyday speech '유언을 남기다' or '유언을 하다' sounds more natural, while 유언하다 appears more in writing and stories. The honorific form is 유언하시다.

en: be covered up; be concealed; be hidden

examples.en: The cause of the accident was covered up for a long time.

examples.ko: 진실이 은폐되면 같은 일이 또 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the truth is covered up, the same thing can happen again.
The concealed facts were reported in the news.

examples.ko: 문제가 은폐되지 않도록 모든 기록을 남겨요.
examples.en: We keep every record so that problems aren't covered up.

examples.ko: 그 사건은 회사 안에서 조용히 은폐되고 있었어요.
examples.en: The incident was being quietly covered up inside the company.

examples.ko: 잘못이 은폐될 뻔했는데 직원이 용기를 내서 말했어요.
examples.en: The mistake almost got covered up, but an employee spoke up bravely.

explain: 일부러 숨겨서 알려지지 않게 되는 경우에 써요. 잘못이나 사고, 비리처럼 나쁜 일에 주로 쓰고, 그냥 안 보이는 것에는 '가려지다'나 '숨겨지다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It means something gets hidden on purpose so it won't become known, usually wrongdoing, accidents, or corruption. For things that are just out of sight, 가려지다 or 숨겨지다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The company tried to cover up the accident.
Covering up a mistake only gets it found out someday.
He deleted the files and concealed the evidence.

examples.ko: 문제를 은폐하는 것보다 빨리 말하는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It's better to speak up quickly than to cover up a problem.
The person who concealed the facts took responsibility.

examples.ko: 기자들은 숨겨진 진실을 은폐할 수 없다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The reporters said the hidden truth couldn't be covered up.

explain: 나쁜 일이나 잘못을 일부러 숨길 때 써요. '숨기다'는 물건에도 사람에도 일상에서 두루 쓰지만, '은폐하다'는 사건·사고·비리를 알리지 않으려는 무거운 상황에 써요.
explain_en: It means deliberately hiding wrongdoing or mistakes. 숨기다 works for anything in daily life, but 은폐하다 fits heavy situations like incidents, accidents, or corruption that someone doesn't want known.

examples.en: My situation right now is very desperate.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 절박한 목소리가 잊히지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't forget the desperation in that person's voice.

examples.ko: 시험이 며칠 안 남아서 마음이 절박했어요.
examples.en: With only a few days left before the exam, I felt desperate.
I'm begging you desperately, so please help me just once.

examples.ko: 이 일이 가장 절박하다고 생각하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't think this is the most urgent matter.

examples.ko: 절박한 사람일수록 작은 도움에도 크게 고마워해요.
examples.en: The more desperate a person is, the more thankful they are for even small help.

explain: '급하다'는 시간이 부족한 느낌이고, '절박하다'는 더 이상 물러설 곳이 없어서 마음이 조이는 느낌이에요. 상황, 심정, 목소리처럼 사람의 마음이나 사정에 쓰는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: 급하다 means there isn't much time, while 절박하다 means there is no room left to back away and the heart feels squeezed. It is often used for a situation, a state of mind, or a voice.

en: be founded (of a team, orchestra, etc.)

examples.en: A new baseball team was founded in our city.
The choir was founded ten years ago.
A women's soccer team is scheduled to be founded next year.

examples.ko: 창단된 지 얼마 안 된 팀이라서 응원이 필요해요.
examples.en: It's a newly founded team, so it needs support.
I remember the day the orchestra was founded.

examples.ko: 학교에 응원단이 창단되고 나서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The mood got better after a cheering squad was founded at school.

explain: 스포츠 팀, 합창단, 오케스트라처럼 '단'이 붙는 단체가 만들어질 때만 써요. 회사는 '설립되다', 학교는 '개교하다', 가게는 '문을 열다'라고 달라요.
explain_en: Use it only for groups ending in 단, such as sports teams, choirs, and orchestras. Companies are 설립되다, schools are 개교하다, and shops simply 문을 열다.

examples.en: The city founded a new soccer team.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 모여서 합창단을 창단하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Neighbors got together and decided to start a choir.
The school is founding a baseball club for the first time this year.
That coach is the person who founded the team.
To start an orchestra, you first need members.

examples.ko: 저는 대학 때 밴드를 창단할 생각이었어요.
examples.en: In college I was planning to form a band.

explain: 팀이나 합창단, 악단처럼 '단'이 붙는 단체를 처음 만들 때 써요. 회사를 만들 때는 '설립하다'나 '세우다'라고 해요. 팀이 처음 생기는 일은 주로 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is used when you start a group ending in 단, such as a team, choir, or orchestra. For a company, say 설립하다 or 세우다. You hear it most often in sports news about new teams.

examples.ko: 집을 사서 되팔려고 투기하는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people speculate by buying houses to resell them.
He made a lot of money speculating in land.
The government cracks down on people who speculate in real estate.
He lost all his assets speculating in stocks.
I don't speculate; I save slowly.

examples.ko: 투기할 돈이 있으면 먼저 빚부터 갚으세요.
examples.en: If you have money to speculate with, pay off your debts first.

explain: 집값이나 땅값이 오를 것을 보고 싼 값에 사서 나중에 비싸게 팔려는 행동을 말할 때 써요. '투자하다'와 달리 대개 안 좋은 시선이 담겨 있어요. 보통 '부동산 투기'처럼 명사와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes buying cheap in hopes that prices rise and selling high later, usually with a negative tone. Unlike 투자하다, it often carries criticism. It most commonly appears as the noun phrase '부동산 투기'.

en: endless; very many; long-lasting (used only in a fixed phrase for 'day after day')

examples.en: I work overtime day after day, so I'm exhausted.
My brother does nothing but play games all the time.

examples.ko: 허구한 날 늦는 친구를 기다리기 지쳤어요.
examples.en: I'm tired of waiting for a friend who is late every single day.

examples.ko: 허구한 날 비가 와서 빨래를 못 말려요.
examples.en: It rains day after day, so I can't dry my laundry.

examples.ko: 왜 허구한 날 같은 반찬만 먹어요?
examples.en: Why do we eat the same side dishes every single day?

examples.ko: 허구한 날 싸우는 부부를 보면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to see a couple who argue day after day.

explain: 거의 항상 '허구한 날'이라는 덩어리로만 쓰고, 불평하는 느낌이 들어요. '매일'은 그냥 사실을 말하지만, '허구한 날'은 지겹고 짜증 난다는 마음이 들어가 있어요. 혼자 '허구해요'라고 말하는 일은 거의 없어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the fixed chunk '허구한 날' and carries a complaining tone. 매일 just states a fact, while 허구한 날 adds the feeling of being fed up. People hardly ever say '허구해요' alone.

examples.ko: 밤에 형광 조끼를 입으면 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: A fluorescent vest makes you easy to spot at night.
I marked the important parts of my notebook with a highlighter.

examples.ko: 이 스티커는 어두운 곳에서 형광으로 빛나요.
examples.en: This sticker glows fluorescent in the dark.
The fluorescent light on the ceiling is flickering and hurts my eyes.
My younger brother bought neon pink sneakers.

examples.ko: 형광 물감은 어두운 방에서 더 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: Fluorescent paint looks prettier in a dark room.

explain: '형광펜', '형광등', '형광색'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 나오는 일이 많아요. 형광펜은 줄을 칠 때, 형광등은 천장 전등을 가리키고, 형광색은 눈에 확 띄는 밝은 색이에요.
explain_en: It usually attaches to other words, as in 형광펜 (highlighter), 형광등 (fluorescent light), and 형광색 (neon color). It is rarely used alone in daily speech.

examples.en: Dust is sucked into the vacuum cleaner.
It is dangerous if smoke is inhaled into the body.
Air is being drawn in through this hole.

examples.ko: 흡입된 가루가 폐에 쌓일 수 있어요.
examples.en: The inhaled powder can build up in the lungs.
There was an accident where clothing got sucked into a machine.

examples.ko: 독한 가스가 흡입되지 않게 마스크를 쓰세요.
examples.en: Wear a mask so that toxic gas isn't inhaled.

explain: 공기, 연기, 먼지 같은 것이 몸이나 기계 안으로 빨려 들어올 때 써요. '들이마시다'는 사람이 하는 행동이고, '흡입되다'는 그 결과를 설명하는 말이라 의학이나 안전 안내문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes air, smoke, or dust being drawn into a body or machine. 들이마시다 is what a person does, whereas 흡입되다 describes the result and appears often in medical or safety notices.

examples.en: I wear a mask so I don't inhale dust.
This vacuum cleaner sucks up even tiny bits of trash.

examples.ko: 의사가 약을 흡입하는 방법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me how to inhale the medicine.
I inhaled a lot of smoke and now I'm coughing.

examples.ko: 기계가 공기를 흡입한 다음 필터로 걸러요.
examples.en: The machine takes in air and then filters it.

examples.ko: 약을 깊게 흡입했다가 천천히 숨을 내쉬세요.
examples.en: Inhale the medicine deeply, then breathe out slowly.

explain: '들이마시다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 의사의 설명이나 안전 안내, 기계 설명서에 자주 나와요. 사람이 숨을 쉬는 것뿐 아니라 청소기나 기계가 공기나 먼지를 빨아들일 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is a stiffer word than 들이마시다 and shows up in doctors' explanations, safety notices, and machine manuals. It covers both people breathing something in and machines like vacuum cleaners drawing in air or dust.

en: dismissal (of a legal claim or petition)

examples.en: The court dismissed this lawsuit.
The application was rejected because of missing documents.
A decision to dismiss this case was issued.

examples.ko: 변호사는 각하를 받아들일 수 없다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The lawyer said he couldn't accept the dismissal.

examples.ko: 항소가 각하 판결을 받아서 다시 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: The appeal got a dismissal ruling, so we have to prepare again.
Please check what the reason for the dismissal is.

explain: 법원이나 관청에서 신청이나 소송을 들어보지 않고 돌려보낼 때 쓰는 법률 용어예요. 내용을 보고 '안 된다'고 하는 '기각'과 달라요. 대통령에게 쓰던 높임말 '각하'와 소리만 같고 뜻은 전혀 달라요.
explain_en: It is a legal term for when a court or office turns away a claim without examining its substance, which differs from 기각 (rejecting after review). It shares only its sound with the old honorific 각하 once used for presidents.

examples.en: The application was dismissed because of incomplete documents.

examples.ko: 소송이 각하되면 처음부터 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: If the lawsuit is dismissed, you have to start over.
I'm worried that the claim will be dismissed.

examples.ko: 각하된 사건은 다시 접수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A dismissed case can be filed again.
I got word that the objection was dismissed.
It ended up being dismissed because the deadline had passed.

explain: 법원이나 관청이 신청이나 소송을 내용도 보지 않고 돌려보낼 때 써요. 서류가 빠졌거나 기한을 넘겼을 때 자주 일어나고, 내용을 보고 거절하는 '기각되다'와 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when a court or office returns a petition or lawsuit without examining its content, often due to missing documents or a missed deadline. It differs from 기각되다, where the content is reviewed and then rejected.

examples.en: The court dismissed the lawsuit.

examples.ko: 재판부는 서류가 부족하다며 신청을 각하할 수 있어요.
examples.en: The court can dismiss the petition, saying documents are missing.

examples.ko: 관청에서 제 신청을 각하해서 다시 접수했어요.
examples.en: The office turned down my application, so I filed it again.

examples.ko: 법원이 청구를 각하하면 이유를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: When the court dismisses a claim, it tells you the reason.
The committee decided to dismiss that request.
The judge explained why he dismissed it.

explain: 법원이나 관청이 신청이나 소송을 내용 판단 없이 돌려보낼 때 써요. 일상에서 거절할 때는 '거절하다'나 '안 받아 주다'를 쓰고, '각하하다'는 법률 뉴스에서만 거의 나와요.
explain_en: Used when a court or office returns a petition or lawsuit without ruling on its merits. In daily life you'd say 거절하다 for refusing; 각하하다 appears almost only in legal news.

examples.ko: 저는 늦으면 안 된다는 강박이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a compulsion that I must never be late.

examples.ko: 시험 전에는 완벽해야 한다는 강박 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: Before exams I can't sleep because of the compulsion to be perfect.

examples.ko: 그는 손을 자꾸 씻는 강박이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a compulsion to wash his hands again and again.

examples.ko: 강박 때문에 문을 잠갔는지 계속 확인해요.
examples.en: Because of my compulsion, I keep checking whether I locked the door.

examples.ko: 일을 다 해야 한다는 강박에서 벗어나고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get free from the compulsion to finish all the work.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 이겨야 한다는 강박으로 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: The player struggled under the pressure of having to win.

explain: '강박'은 '~해야 한다'는 생각에서 벗어나지 못하는 마음의 상태예요. 보통 '강박증', '강박 관념'처럼 쓰고, 단순히 바쁜 것과는 달라요. 조금 심하게 느껴질 때 쓰는 말이라 가볍게 쓰면 안 돼요.
explain_en: It describes a state of mind stuck on 'I must do this', usually in the forms 강박증 or 강박 관념. It is not the same as being busy, and it sounds heavy, so avoid using it lightly.

examples.en: This problem was examined in depth in the paper.

examples.ko: 여러 가지 원인이 이 연구에서 고찰돼요.
examples.en: Several causes are examined in this study.

examples.ko: 충분히 고찰된 결론이라서 믿을 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a thoroughly examined conclusion, so you can trust it.

examples.ko: 다음 장에서는 이 현상이 고찰될 거예요.
examples.en: This phenomenon will be examined in the next chapter.
The historical background has to be examined first.
It's a pity the opinion wasn't examined thoroughly.

explain: 논문이나 보고서에서 어떤 주제가 깊이 살펴보고 연구될 때 써요. 말로는 거의 안 하고 글에서만 보여요. 일상에서는 '생각해 보다', '살펴보다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used in papers and reports when a topic is studied and examined in depth. It is almost never spoken and appears only in writing. In daily life people say 생각해 보다 or 살펴보다.

examples.en: This paper examines Korean honorifics in depth.
I looked deeply into environmental problems.

examples.ko: 그 원인을 고찰하려면 자료가 더 필요해요.
examples.en: To study the cause closely, we need more data.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생들에게 작품의 의미를 고찰하게 했어요.
examples.en: The teacher had the students reflect closely on the meaning of the work.

examples.ko: 연구자는 오랜 시간 이 현상을 고찰한 끝에 결론을 냈어요.
examples.en: After studying this phenomenon for a long time, the researcher reached a conclusion.
I want to write a piece that reflects deeply on life.

explain: 어떤 주제를 깊이 살펴보고 생각하거나 연구할 때 써요. 논문, 보고서, 칼럼 같은 글에서 주로 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '생각해 보다'나 '살펴보다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when examining and thinking about a topic in depth, mainly in papers, reports, and columns. In daily conversation 생각해 보다 or 살펴보다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The tax is paid automatically.
The tuition has not been paid yet.
When the fee is paid, they let you know by text message.

examples.ko: 기한 안에 납부된 금액은 돌려받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: The amount paid within the deadline cannot be refunded.
The insurance premium is paid from my salary every month.
I confirmed that the fine had been paid.

explain: 세금, 등록금, 보험료, 벌금처럼 기관에 내는 돈이 처리됐을 때 써요. 가게에서 물건값을 내는 것에는 쓰지 않고 '결제되다'를 써요. 내는 사람이 주어면 '납부하다'예요.
explain_en: Used when money owed to an institution, such as taxes, tuition, insurance, or fines, has been paid. For paying at a shop use 결제되다 instead. When the payer is the subject, it is 납부하다.

examples.en: The company is looking for a new way.

examples.ko: 문제를 해결할 방법을 함께 모색해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's look for a way to solve the problem together.
He explored starting a business instead of getting a job.
More people are seeking change.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 협력 방안을 모색하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries decided to explore ways to cooperate.
We need time to look for alternatives.

explain: '찾다'는 물건이나 사람에게도 쓰지만 '모색하다'는 해결 방법, 대안, 길처럼 아직 정해지지 않은 것을 찾을 때만 써요. 뉴스, 회의, 보고서에 자주 나오고 말투가 딱딱해요.
explain_en: 찾다 works for objects and people, but 모색하다 is used only for things not yet settled, such as solutions, alternatives, or a path forward. It is a formal word common in news, meetings, and reports.

examples.en: He has adored her for a long time.

examples.ko: 저는 그 가수를 사모하는 마음으로 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote a letter with the heart of someone who adores that singer.

examples.ko: 시인은 멀리 있는 사람을 사모하며 시를 지었어요.
examples.en: The poet wrote a poem longing for someone far away.
The senior I secretly adored has graduated.
I turned away without being able to say that I adored him.
Many disciples looked up to their teacher with deep affection.

explain: '좋아하다'보다 훨씬 깊고 조심스러운, 짝사랑에 가까운 마음이에요. 일상 대화보다 시, 소설, 노래 가사에서 더 자주 나오는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. 지금은 '좋아하다'나 '짝사랑하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a far deeper, more reserved feeling than 좋아하다, close to unrequited love. It has an old-fashioned feel and appears more in poems, novels, and lyrics than in daily talk. Today people more often say 좋아하다 or 짝사랑하다.

examples.ko: 할머니의 슬기 덕분에 어려운 시기를 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my grandmother's wisdom, we got through hard times.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 우리가 슬기를 모아서 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: We have to pool our wisdom to solve this.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 슬기가 남달라서 어른들도 놀랐어요.
examples.en: That child had such rare good sense that even adults were surprised.

examples.ko: 옛사람들의 슬기를 배울 수 있는 책이에요.
examples.en: It's a book where you can learn the wisdom of people of old.
He showed good sense in the crisis and saved everyone.

examples.ko: 슬기와 용기가 있으면 두려울 게 없어요.
examples.en: With wisdom and courage, there's nothing to fear.

explain: '지혜'와 거의 같지만 '슬기'는 어려운 상황을 잘 풀어 가는 실제적인 재치에 더 가까워요. '슬기롭다'로 자주 쓰고, '슬기를 발휘하다', '슬기를 모으다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: Nearly the same as 지혜, but 슬기 leans toward the practical cleverness of handling difficult situations well. It often appears as 슬기롭다 and in phrases like 슬기를 발휘하다 and 슬기를 모으다.

examples.ko: 여름에 따 먹은 오디가 정말 달았어요.
examples.en: The mulberries I picked and ate in summer were really sweet.
If you eat mulberries, your lips turn black.
My grandmother made me jam from mulberries.

examples.ko: 시장에서 신선한 오디를 한 상자 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a box of fresh mulberries at the market.

examples.ko: 오디 열매가 익으면 나무 아래가 보랏빛이 돼요.
examples.en: When the mulberries ripen, the ground beneath the tree turns purple.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친구와 오디를 따러 다녔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I went out picking mulberries with my friends.

explain: 뽕나무의 열매를 가리켜요. 초여름에 열리고 익으면 짙은 보라색이 되어서 먹으면 입술이 물들어요. 잼이나 주스로도 만들어 먹어요.
explain_en: It is the fruit of the mulberry tree. It ripens in early summer and turns deep purple, staining your lips when you eat it, and it is also made into jam or juice.

en: finish a race; complete the whole course

examples.en: This time I completed the full marathon.
My goal is to run all the way to the end.
My legs hurt, but I finished without giving up.
Next year I want to complete the ten-kilometer run.
They give a medal to everyone who finishes.
Even in the rain, the runners finished the whole course.

explain: 달리기, 자전거, 경주 같은 길을 처음부터 끝까지 다 마쳤을 때 써요. 등수와 상관없이 포기하지 않고 끝까지 갔다는 뿌듯함이 들어 있어요. 책을 끝까지 읽는 건 '완독하다', 드라마를 몰아 보는 건 '정주행하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when you finish a whole route in running, cycling, or a race, regardless of your rank. It carries pride in not giving up. For finishing a book use 완독하다, and for binge-watching a drama use 정주행하다.

examples.en: They repainted the exterior wall of the building.
The outer wall is cracked, so rain leaks in.

examples.ko: 아파트 외벽 공사 때문에 소리가 커요.
examples.en: It's loud because of the exterior wall work at the apartment.
Ivy is growing on the outside wall.
In winter, a house with thick outer walls is warm.
Workers hang from ropes to clean the exterior wall.

explain: 건물의 바깥쪽을 둘러싼 벽이에요. 반대말은 안쪽의 '내벽'이에요. 공사나 건축 이야기에 자주 나오고, 평소에는 그냥 '벽'이라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: It is the wall on the outside of a building, and its opposite is 내벽, the inner wall. It appears in construction talk, though in casual speech people often just say 벽.

examples.en: The spy's infiltration was only discovered later.
The reporter did undercover reporting inside the factory.

examples.ko: 경찰이 범인의 잠입 경로를 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are investigating the culprit's route of entry.

examples.ko: 영화 속 잠입 장면이 정말 긴장돼요.
examples.en: The infiltration scene in the movie is really tense.

examples.ko: 건물 경비는 잠입을 막으려고 문을 늘 잠가요.
examples.en: The building's guards always lock the doors to prevent anyone sneaking in.
The infiltration operation was carried out very quietly.

explain: 몰래 들어가는 일을 말해요. 영화, 뉴스, 수사 이야기에서 자주 나오고 '잠입 취재', '잠입 수사'처럼 목적이 있는 경우가 많아요. 그냥 몰래 들어가는 것은 '몰래 들어가다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It refers to entering somewhere secretly, and appears in films, news, and investigations, often in set phrases like 잠입 취재 (undercover reporting) and 잠입 수사 (undercover investigation). For plainly sneaking in, 몰래 들어가다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: A reporter infiltrated the company and exposed its secrets.
A thief sneaked into the house at night.

examples.ko: 형사는 조직에 잠입하기 위해 신분을 숨겼어요.
examples.en: The detective hid his identity in order to infiltrate the organization.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 적의 기지에 잠입해요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie infiltrates the enemy base.
The person who sneaked in was caught right away.
Who could have sneaked into the building?

explain: '들어가다'에 몰래, 목적을 숨기고 간다는 뜻이 더 들어 있어요. 스파이, 기자, 형사, 도둑이 주어로 자주 나와요. 허락 없이 들어가는 '침입하다'는 부수고 들어가는 느낌, '잠입하다'는 들키지 않으려는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It adds the sense of going in secretly, with a hidden purpose, to 들어가다. Spies, reporters, detectives, and thieves are common subjects. 침입하다 feels like breaking in, whereas 잠입하다 feels like trying not to be noticed.

examples.en: I was caught speeding.
A shop that sold fake goods was exposed.

examples.ko: 시험에서 부정행위를 하다 적발되면 점수를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you are caught cheating on an exam, you lose your score.

examples.ko: 세금을 속인 회사가 적발되었다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a company that cheated on taxes had been caught.

examples.ko: 몰래 쓰레기를 버리다가 적발되지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get caught dumping trash secretly.
If you break the rules, you can be caught.

explain: 숨기던 잘못이나 법·규정을 어긴 일이 조사나 단속으로 드러났을 때 써요. 단속, 검사, 점검과 자주 같이 나와요. 그냥 들키는 일은 '들키다'가 일상에서 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when a hidden wrongdoing or a violation of laws or rules comes to light through inspection or enforcement. It often pairs with 단속, 검사, and 점검. For simply being found out in daily life, 들키다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The police caught a speeding car.
Customs caught illegal goods.

examples.ko: 검사관은 위생 문제를 적발하면 영업을 멈추게 해요.
examples.en: If an inspector finds hygiene violations, they have the business stop operating.

examples.ko: 부정 행위를 적발한 직원에게 상을 주었어요.
examples.en: They gave an award to the employee who exposed the fraud.

examples.ko: 단속반이 불법 주차를 적발하려고 거리를 돌아요.
examples.en: The enforcement team goes around the street to catch illegal parking.
You need evidence when you expose a wrongdoing.

explain: 감추어진 잘못이나 법 위반을 조사해서 찾아낼 때 써요. 주어는 경찰, 세관, 검사관처럼 단속하는 쪽이에요. 위반한 쪽이 당하면 '적발되다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used when finding hidden wrongdoing or legal violations through investigation. The subject is usually the enforcing side, such as police, customs, or inspectors. If the offender is the focus, use 적발되다.

examples.ko: 건강과 직결된 문제라서 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: This is directly linked to health, so we need to be careful.
This road is directly connected to the airport.

examples.ko: 안전과 직결되는 일은 서두르면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Things directly tied to safety must not be rushed.
Salary is directly tied to daily life, so it matters.
This subway station connects straight to the department store.

examples.ko: 결과가 성적과 직결되어서 모두 열심히 해요.
examples.en: The result is directly tied to grades, so everyone works hard.

explain: '~와 직결되다' 꼴로 자주 써요. 길이나 건물이 곧바로 이어졌다는 뜻도 있고, 문제나 일이 곧바로 영향을 준다는 비유로도 많이 써요. '관계있다'보다 연결이 훨씬 가깝고 강한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Most often used as '~와 직결되다'. It can mean a road or building is joined straight to another, or, figuratively, that one issue directly affects another. The link feels much closer and stronger than 관계있다.

examples.en: Don't tie grades directly to happiness.

examples.ko: 두 사건을 직결시켜서 생각하면 오해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you link the two incidents directly, you can misunderstand.
The company tied performance directly to pay.
It's a stretch to link those two directly.
They built a road that connects the airport directly to downtown.

examples.ko: 모든 문제를 돈과 직결시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't need to link every problem directly to money.

explain: 원인과 결과나 두 일을 바로 이어서 생각하거나 만들 때 써요. 주로 '~을 ~와 직결시키다' 꼴이고, 너무 단순하게 연결한다는 안 좋은 느낌으로 쓸 때도 많아요. 스스로 이어진다는 '직결되다'와 달라요.
explain_en: Used when you link two things directly in thought or in practice, in the form '~을 ~와 직결시키다', and often implies the link is too simple. It differs from 직결되다, where things are connected by themselves.
